A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Agent Rosetta work and contain readable text, figures, tables, and appendices. Retained appendix material can be matched across renumbering; no material reading gaps prevent comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on composition-penalty generation, canonical protein sequence design, and TRF insertion, including numerical results in its appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds environment ablations, expanded baseline comparisons, and molecular-dynamics simulation outcomes.

M1.justification: The proposed interaction loop, three action types, simplified syntax, Pareto selection, prompts, and action templates are retained. The smaller LLM evaluation and withholding of ESMFold feedback are experimental variants; no revision to the proposed framework is established.

E1.justification: The same eight canonical-design backbones and four TRF-insertion proteins are retained. New Appendix C expands diagnostic task coverage to custom score functions, sequence extraction, per-residue energy reporting, and cavity-volume/radius-of-gyration calculations under differing prompting support.

E2.justification: v2 adds BoltzGen and a randomized scripted policy to the canonical-design comparisons, retaining ProteinMPNN, both fixed human protocols, and the existing naive policy. Appendix E.5 additionally evaluates two manual revisions of the human protocol on 9KGY and 9C14. These substantially broaden the comparison methods.

E3.justification: Section 3.2 replaces the reported 128-design comparator trials with matched total budgets of approximately 2048 candidates and removes the stated pLDDT >=85 filtering rule. v2 also evaluates Qwen3 30B, introduces canonical-design AF3 validation of selected top-10 designs, and adds 1-microsecond MD validation protocols. These are reported protocol changes, without establishing that every retained experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds prompt-only environment ablations, an experiment withholding ESMFold metrics from Qwen3 235B, iterative human-protocol analysis, and MD stability checks for both protein-design tasks. The ESMFold ablation reports changes below 0.1 angstrom RMSD and 1% pLDDT. These substantially extend the investigation of environment necessity, feedback dependence, and design stability.

E5.justification: The existing 16-trial, 1000-bootstrap, best-of-eight reporting remains. v2 adds three independent MD replicates with different initial velocities, MD confidence intervals, and paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests with family-wise error control at 0.05. This introduces inferential testing beyond v1's descriptive uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Canonical results are revised under changed protocols: aggregate GPT-5 RMSD changes from 639 to 608 milliangstroms and ProteinMPNN from 570 to 581 (v1 Table C.2; v2 Table E.3). New results include ablations, comparators, and MD outcomes, including NCAA median RMSD of 2.6 versus 3.1 angstroms for GPT-5 and the human baseline. Original NCAA AF3 scores are retained. The narrative changes its win count from five to four backbones, although v2 Table E.2 still shows an agent variant leading on five.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal theorems or proofs, and the retained method and syntax descriptions introduce no changed mathematical reasoning. The new stability measurements and statistical tests are evaluation additions.

C1.justification: The abstract and central claims about structured environments, accessibility, and competitive protein design remain unchanged. The introduction and conclusion modestly broaden the explicit performance-parity claim from ProteinMPNN to ProteinMPNN and BoltzGen.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands interpretation and limitations: it identifies self-correction loops, explains how TRF insertion can relocate the protein core, and discusses smaller-model failures. The conclusion explicitly limits evidence to RosettaScripts and a few structures and conditions expected generalization on scientific knowledge and structured interfaces. A new impact statement addresses misuse and confidently wrong designs.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-code link and a detailed MD appendix specifying OpenMM 8.2, VMD 1.9.3, CHARMM36, solvation and ion settings, integration parameters, and equilibration procedures. It also discloses OpenRouter provider selection and clarifies model sizes. Existing prompts, XML templates, preprocessing descriptions, and TRF parameters are retained.

R1.justification: The introduction newly distinguishes low-level scientific-software integration from high-level orchestration, including ProtAgents and Agent Laboratory. References add BoltzGen and MD-related works and remove the mixed-chirality macrocycle paper. Appendix A's broader positioning remains largely unchanged; bibliographic metadata expansions do not constitute new research coverage.

P1.justification: The main narrative and most appendix prose are retained. v2 edits comparison and evaluation passages, separates the NCAA comparison/evaluation discussion, adds an impact statement and dedicated ablation/MD appendices, and updates affiliations and model terminology. The changes do not amount to a wholesale language or structural rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 redraws Figure 1, separates and resizes previously paired main-text figures, reorganizes the canonical trajectory grid, and changes table ordering and column structure. New displays include the environment-ablation table, MD summary table, and three MD trajectory figures. These substantially revise the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evidence behind the original claims through environment and feedback ablations, broader comparisons, matched candidate budgets, canonical AF3 validation, and replicated MD checks for both design tasks. These address important weaknesses in v1's validation and controls. Small protein sets, limited human iteration, and the inconsistent backbone win-count summary remain weaknesses, but do not outweigh the gains. The added stability evidence remains computational rather than experimental validation of synthesized proteins.
